transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?
I’m exhausted all the time, like I’m worn out before the day even starts, and I can’t seem to get my energy back. Even when I try to rest or sleep in on weekends, I still feel completely drained.
How long have you been feeling this tired and down, and have you had similar episodes like this before that got better and then came back?

It all started about seven or eight months ago when I transitioned into my full-time lab job, and it has been pretty constant ever since. I’ve never really experienced anything like this before, so it’s a completely new struggle for me.
During these past 7–8 months, have you felt depressed or down most days nearly every day, or has it been more of a low mood that comes and goes?
I wouldn't really say I feel depressed or sad, to be honest. It's more that I feel completely exhausted and drained all the time because my mind is constantly overwhelmed by worry and anxiety.

Did the anxiety and exhaustion start mainly after a specific stressful event or major life change, and has it improved at all since then? Or do you find yourself worrying about many different things most days, even when there isn’t one clear trigger?

It definitely started when I transitioned to my full-time lab job about eight months ago, and it hasn't gotten any better. While that job change was the initial trigger, my worry has since expanded to almost everything—I constantly spiral over minor lab mistakes, losing my job, paying rent, and my parents' health back in El Salvador, even when there's no immediate reason to worry.
Do you also have physical anxiety symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, trouble concentrating, irritability, or sleep problems most days?

Yes, I feel constantly wound up and restless, like I'm pacing around the lab or bouncing my leg all day. My muscles are also incredibly tight—my shoulders and neck get so knotted by the evening, and my jaw always aches from clenching.
Do you have trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or waking up feeling unrefreshed because of the worry most nights?

Yes, I constantly wake up feeling completely unrefreshed, almost like I've pulled an all-nighter in the lab even when I sleep for many hours. Even if my body crashes, my mind is always racing with worries about my lab work and my family back home. It feels like my brain never actually rests, which leaves me exhausted before the day even begins.

Did these symptoms start within a few months of the job change and feel mainly tied to that stressor, or have you had ongoing excessive worry about many areas of life for most days over the past 6 months even beyond that trigger?

Yes, it started right with the job transition about eight months ago, but it has definitely expanded far beyond just work stress. For most of the past six months, I've had constant, daily worries about my parents' health in El Salvador, paying rent, and my overall future. It has become an ongoing struggle that I can't seem to turn off, regardless of how things are going at the lab.
Over the past 6 months, have you found it very hard to control or stop the worrying most days, even when you know there is no immediate problem?

Yes, once the worries start, they completely take over and I just can't shut them off. Even when I try to relax, watch a game, or video chat with my family, my mind just spirals back to those anxious thoughts. This has been happening almost every single day for the past seven or eight months.

Have you ever had sudden panic attacks, with a rush of intense fear that peaks within minutes and includes symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, sweating, or a feeling that something terrible is about to happen?

No, I've never had those sudden, overwhelming panic attacks with chest pain or shortness of breath. Instead, my anxiety is more of a constant, heavy background worry and physical tension that just stays with me all day.
Have you also noticed any of these most days: feeling unusually on edge or keyed up, being easily fatigued, trouble concentrating or your mind going blank, irritability, or muscle tension?

I definitely feel easily fatigued and constantly keyed up, almost like I've had way too much coffee, which leaves my shoulders, neck, and jaw incredibly tense. I haven't really noticed my mind going blank or being irritable, but the physical tension and exhaustion are constant.

opening_question.question: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The presentation is most consistent with generalized anxiety disorder: excessive anxiety and worry about multiple areas of life for at least 6 months, difficulty controlling the worry, and associated symptoms including restlessness, muscle tension, fatigue, and unrefreshing sleep. Symptoms are persistent, pervasive beyond the initial job stressor, and cause clear exhaustion and impairment in daily functioning.
